mid-document-section-missing-heading: A page split into topical sections gives most of them real headings, but one substantial section is left un-headed, so a screen-reader user can't find or label it.
visual-only-section-boundaries-no-headin: Sections are shown only through visual styling like cards, columns, colour bands or whitespace, with no heading markup, so a screen-reader user perceives one undifferentiated blob.
heading-text-mismatched-or-generic: A section's heading text is wrong, copy-pasted, or a vague placeholder like 'More', so it doesn't actually name the section and gives a screen-reader user no orientation.
multiple-navigation-regions-unheaded: A page has several distinct navigation areas (top nav, sidebar, footer links) but none has a heading, so a screen-reader user can't tell them apart when jumping by heading.
semantic-heading-level-mismatch: Heading levels don't match the real content hierarchy, so a sub-topic reads as a sibling or two equal sections read as parent-and-child, confusing how a screen-reader user understands structure.
nameless-heading-element: A heading element exists but holds only whitespace, a decorative image, or ornamental glyphs, so a screen-reader user hears 'heading' with no name and gains no orientation.
aaa-inapplicable-unsectioned-prose: A page is genuinely one continuous document like a letter or narrative with no real sections, so it correctly needs no section headings and should not be flagged as a failure.
